inline_comments.comment: The function silently returns with no output and no error when the framework isn't `@storybook/react-vite`. Users running `storybook ai init` on Angular, Vue, React+Webpack, or any other project will get zero feedback — no message, no exit code, nothing. Add a `logger.warn` or `logger.error` explaining which frameworks are supported and call `process.exit(1)`. The restriction should also be documented in the command description string and `--help` output.

The generated code block is labeled ` ```ts ` and shows the filename as `preview.ts`, but its decorator body uses JSX (`<ThemeProvider>`, `<MemoryRouter>`, `<Story />`). TypeScript refuses JSX in `.ts` files — the file extension must be `.tsx`. Both branches of `getPreviewConfigExample` (the CSF-factory branch here and the standard branch around line 163) have this same defect. Fix by changing `preview.ts` → `preview.tsx` and the code-fence language tag to ` ```tsx `.

The generated import path is constructed as `'@storybook/${renderer}'` where `renderer` comes from `data.rendererPackage`. The explore-agent confirmed that `rendererPackage` returns the full scoped package name (e.g. `@storybook/react`), so the template produces the nonsensical path `from '@storybook/@storybook/react'`. Since the command is currently gated to `@storybook/react-vite` projects, renderer will always be `@storybook/react`. Fix by stripping the prefix — e.g. `renderer.replace(/^@storybook\//, '')` — before interpolating, so the import reads `from '@storybook/react'`.

`std-env` is not listed in `code/lib/create-storybook/package.json`'s `dependencies` (confirmed by the explore agent — the only runtime deps are `semver` and `storybook`). This import will throw `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at runtime once the package is published. Add `std-env` to the package's `dependencies`.

`detectAgent()` is called here unconditionally, before the `if (isAgent)` guard. In `std-env`, `detectAgent()` returns `null` when no agent is active — calling `.name` on `null` produces `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name')` for every ordinary user running `npx create storybook`. Even if the return type were non-null, this line logs `'Detecting agent presence: ...'` to every user's terminal — it is debug output that must not appear in production. Remove the line, or at minimum move it inside the `if (isAgent)` block.

`promptAiSetup` returns `true` (opt-in) whenever `skipPrompt` is `true`. The explore agent confirmed that `skipPrompt` is `!isInteractive || !!options.yes`, so any user passing `--yes` / `-y` will silently get `Feature.AI` selected and `@storybook/addon-mcp` installed without ever seeing the question. Non-interactive defaults for a new feature should be opt-out (`return false`), not opt-in. Users who want AI setup should be required to explicitly request it.

This dynamic import uses a deep relative path that crosses package boundaries (`../../cli-storybook/src/ai`). Per project conventions, one monorepo package must import from another via the public package export path (e.g. a `@storybook/cli-storybook` entry point), not a relative deep path into another package's `src/`. Deep cross-package relative imports are fragile under restructuring and bypass the package's intended API surface.
`detectAgent()` is invoked a second time here (first call is at line 126). Cache the result in a variable — e.g. `const agentInfo = detectAgent();` — and reference `agentInfo` in both log calls.

`@storybook/addon-mcp` is pushed onto the `addons` array without first checking whether it is already present (e.g. if the user explicitly listed it in their config). Per project rules, before conditionally pushing a package specifier onto an addon array, strip version suffixes and verify the base package name is not already in the list to avoid duplicate or conflicting entries.

Per project conventions, every new enum member (and every entry in `features` blocks on public interfaces) should be preceded by a JSDoc comment explaining its purpose. `AI = 'ai'` has none. Add a brief `/** Enables AI-assisted setup flow, installs @storybook/addon-mcp */` above the entry.

The `agent` property uses an inline `//` comment instead of JSDoc. Per project conventions, optional properties on public TypeScript interfaces should be documented with `/** … */`. Additionally, the comment text contains a typo / capitalisation inconsistency: `ai agent` should be `AI agent`.

The `dedent` template literal is misused: content starts inline on the same line as the opening backtick (`dedent\`Would you like…`), while the second line inherits its full source indentation. Because `ts-dedent` strips the *minimum* indentation across all non-empty lines, and the first line has zero leading spaces, nothing is stripped — the second line renders with several leading spaces in the prompt. Use the conventional form with a newline after the backtick so both lines share the same indentation and `dedent` strips it correctly:

```ts
dedent`
  Would you like to improve your Storybook setup with AI?
  We will provide you with a prompt…
`
```

general_comments.comment: `isAgent` from `std-env` detects CI/CD automation runners (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, CircleCI, etc.) — not AI coding assistants (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot Terminal). Any `npx create storybook` invoked inside a GitHub Actions workflow will have `isAgent === true`, causing `options.agent = true` to be set, `options.yes` to be force-enabled in `doInitiate`, dev-server startup to be suppressed, and `@storybook/addon-mcp` to be installed silently. The codebase already ships `code/core/src/telemetry/detect-agent.ts` with its own `KnownAgentName` union and `detectExplicitAgent` function for exactly this purpose. Either use that existing utility and extend `KnownAgentName` for the AI assistants of interest in this PR, or — if `std-env` genuinely covers the target assistants — add a code comment citing exactly which environment variables each AI assistant sets and confirming the `std-env` version required.

No automated tests are added (all testing checkboxes are unchecked). The new code includes several independently testable pure functions: `parseMajorVersion`, `getDocsUrl`, `getPrompts`, `generateMarkdownOutput`, `generateJsonOutput`, `promptAiSetup`, and the updated `determineFeatures`. The renderer-import bug and the JSX-in-.ts bug in the generated instructions would both have been caught by snapshot or unit tests against the output strings. At minimum, add unit tests for `generateMarkdownOutput` and `generateJsonOutput` that assert the generated import paths and file extensions are correct.

The `storybook ai init` command currently supports only `@storybook/react-vite`, but neither the command description (`'Generate setup instructions to write stories for real components'`) nor the `--help` output mentions this restriction. Users with Angular, Vue, Svelte, or React+webpack projects will run the command and receive no output and no explanation. Either widen support to additional frameworks/renderers, or add the restriction to the description string and emit a clear, actionable message when an unsupported framework is detected.
